lineage.strategy: Changed source path from repeated financial/design-win/leadership evidence to a fresh operating-regulatory adoption signal: Mobileye's September 10 report citing German KBA permit data for SAE Level 4 testing.

observations.observation: Mobileye reported, citing Germany KBA data, that vehicles using Mobileye Drive represented more than 60% of valid SAE Level 4 testing permits assessed in Germany as of the report date.
observations.whyItMatters: This is materially different evidence from pipeline/design-win claims: it indicates current real-world regulatory testing footprint for Mobileye Drive in a rigorous European L4 environment, supporting execution/validation evidence while not proving commercial revenue or scaled deployment.

factors.name: executionMonitoring
factors.basis: A majority share of valid German L4 testing permits reported from KBA data is evidence of active real-world validation footprint for Mobileye Drive.

factors.name: advancedADASMonetization
factors.basis: Regulatory testing footprint can de-risk technical validation but does not itself establish customer conversion, production volumes, pricing or revenue.

risks.risk: Testing-permit share is not equivalent to commercial deployment share, contracted volume, revenue or profitability and should not be scored as such.

unknowns.unknown: The issuer article does not quantify commercial revenue, fleet scale, customer economics or conversion attributable to the German L4 permits.
The underlying KBA dataset was not independently reproduced in this bounded assist, so the >60% figure retains issuer-mediated regulatory attribution.

recommendation: Use this as source-addressed execution/validation evidence, separate from revenue and valuation inputs. Alpha should retain the distinction between regulatory testing footprint and monetization.
